title: Klaus Weiss and his big band
summary: Holman wrote four charts for Weiss's album and remembers the drummer's booming voice and Buddy Rich style.

blocks.x: Speaking of Germany and speaking of drummers, there‟s an entry here in the catalogue entitled Lightnin‟, the Klaus Weiss big band. It‟s got Jiggs Whigham. But the reason why it caught my eye, it‟s got also Benny Bailey listed and also somebody that I had worked with, Joe Gallardo, who probably was in the Cologne big band too. He was also an expatriate in Europe – in Germany at that time. This date is from Ludwigsburg, from September of 1984. I don‟t know if you were actually involved. They‟ve only got – they have you listed as arranger, but I‟m not sure if you were present on the date.
No, I wasn‟t. I wrote, I think, four charts for the band.
Right. But Klaus Weiss, surprisingly enough, is a drummer. Do you recall him? – speaking of German . . .
Yeah. When he called me up, he had this hearty German-sounding voice. I could imagine the mayor of a small town. What‟s the word for them?
The Burgermeister, with a big stein of beer or something, “Ja, ja, ja, ja.”

He said, “I‟m coming to Los Angeles. I‟d like to meet with you.” Okay. He got here. He was a young guy, trim, but he had that big booming voice. We got along great. We‟d kept in touch through the years. His idol was Buddy – Buddy Rich – and he played like him, which is not really my favorite way a drummer could play. But we got along good. He always got a good band together. Benny Bailey was one of our soloists in Cologne on one of our things. He was tough.
